title: Ring Count
statement: A stump seen from above is the most honest clock a tree keeps. The old rings sit wide apart: a whole life between the agrarian ring and the industrial one. Toward the bark the years crowd in, and the newest ring is a thin bright line laid down this season, so close to the edge that the bark has not had time to grow over it. Below the cut the roots are still drinking. Whoever comes next may read the rings, count them, water the seedling I left at the rim, or draw what the tree sees from underneath.
process: I drew eighteen rings by hand-uneven ellipses, each a little rotated so none sits perfectly inside the last, and let the spacing shrink geometrically toward the bark. The one green ring is the only colour inside the wood. Nothing was inherited; this is a root in both senses.
